title: The Wrong Hymn
premise: When Rafael Winterbourne returns to Winterbourne House to bury his twin brother Aurel, he discovers the coffin holds a stranger wearing his brother's face — and that the family's founding ritual, meant to bind a hungry presence in the mirrors, was never finished. The house's reflections lag one second behind reality, and that second is widening, letting something through that has been impersonating Winters for six generations. Rafael, who copes by documenting everything, realizes his own meticulous records are the only map of the ritual's missing final verse — and that the 'founders' were four servants, not the masters, whose loyalty to each other outlasted their loyalty to the lie. To close the breach he must complete the hymn they left unfinished, choosing truth over the comfortable inheritance of silence, even though finishing it will erase every reflection of himself from the world.
about_author: E. M. Okafor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing estate papers in decaying country houses before turning to fiction. They write horror about families that mistake paperwork for love.

chapters.title: The Second Coffin
chapters.summary: Rafael arrives at Winterbourne House for Aurel's funeral and insists on viewing the body — protocol, documentation, prayer. The corpse wears his brother's face but has Aurel's scar on the wrong cheek. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: grief curdling into dread as the first crack opens in his certainty.

chapters.title: Inventory of a House That Watches
chapters.summary: Rafael catalogs the house room by room, photographing everything, noting that several mirrors are draped or turned to the walls. His aunt Serafina warns him some rooms 'keep their own time.' POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: obsessive comfort of record-keeping masking rising unease.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Rafael catches a mirror reflecting him raising his hand a beat after he does it. He tests it with a metronome; the lag is exactly one second, and growing. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: the scientist's thrill of discovery colliding with animal fear.

chapters.title: What Serafina Won't Say
chapters.summary: Serafina admits the family has 'kept the glass quiet' since 1849 but refuses details, burning a page of the household ledger. Rafael photographs the ashes. POV: Rafael, with a brief flashback from Serafina. Emotional beat: loyalty as a cage; the first hint that truth was traded away deliberately.

chapters.title: The Servants' Hymnal
chapters.summary: In the chapel loft Rafael finds a hand-copied hymnal annotated by four names — Odile, Bram, Tessaly, and Juno — servants, not founders. The final hymn is unfinished, cut off mid-verse. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: wonder; the real story begins surfacing beneath the official one.

chapters.title: Aurel, Breathing
chapters.summary: Rafael sees Aurel standing at the end of the corridor — solid, warm, insisting he never died. But Aurel's reflection doesn't move at all. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: longing weaponized; the thing in the glass knows exactly what he misses.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Reading Odile's diary (interleaved documents), Rafael learns the 1849 ritual: four servants sang the founding hymn to seal a presence the master had invited in, and the price was that one singer be forgotten by everyone who loved her. POV: Rafael via Odile. Emotional beat: found family forged in shared danger.

chapters.title: The Widening Second
chapters.summary: The lag reaches three seconds; Rafael watches his own reflection finish movements he hasn't made yet. A maid's reflection walks out of a mirror and is found dead, smiling. POV: Rafael, then the housekeeper Marta. Emotional beat: the threat stops being theoretical.

chapters.title: Everyone Who Loved Her
chapters.summary: Rafael discovers no portrait, letter, or grave mentions Odile — she paid the forgetting-price, and the hymn requires it again. He rages against a ritual built on erasure. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: moral revolt against the cost of safety.

chapters.title: The Funeral of the Wrong Brother
chapters.summary: At the burial, mourners' reflections sing a hymn no one is singing aloud. Rafael recognizes the melody from the servants' hymnal — the congregation is being used as an unwitting choir. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: public performance of grief hiding private terror.

chapters.title: Bram's Confession
chapters.summary: Hidden in the organ case, Bram's letter confesses they stopped the hymn one verse short because Tessaly refused to let Juno pay the forgetting-price — mercy broke the seal. POV: Rafael via Bram. Emotional beat: the wound in the story is an act of love.

chapters.title: Serafina's Verse
chapters.summary: Confronted, Serafina reveals she is Tessaly's descendant and has spent her life refusing to finish the hymn, keeping the presence half-starved rather than sacrifice anyone. She offers Rafael the missing fourth verse. POV: Serafina. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth finally named as opposites.

chapters.title: The House Remembers Him Wrong
chapters.summary: The house begins editing Rafael out — staff forget his name, photographs blur, his documentation vanishes page by page. The presence is pre-paying his price. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: existential vertigo; his records, his identity, dissolving.

chapters.title: Backup Copies
chapters.summary: Rafael recovers his notes from a locked car outside the grounds where the house's influence fails, and realizes the boundary of the haunting is the boundary of the land. He plans. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: agency reclaimed through method.

chapters.title: Juno's Room
chapters.summary: Behind a bricked wall Rafael finds Juno's preserved room and her own journal: she volunteered willingly, and wrote that being forgotten by the living didn't matter if the ones who mattered remembered. POV: Rafael via Juno. Emotional beat: the theme crystallizes — chosen memory over inherited silence.

chapters.title: The Choir Assembles
chapters.summary: Rafael recruits Serafina, Marta, and the skeptical village priest to sing the completed hymn at midnight; the house fights back, flooding halls with reflections of everyone they've lost. POV: multiple, rotating. Emotional beat: found family forming across generations and bloodlines.

chapters.title: First Verse: What Was Invited
chapters.summary: The ritual begins; the mirrors empty of reflections as the presence gathers into the great hall glass, wearing the faces of every dead Winterbourne, offering each singer their deepest grief. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: temptation staged as reunion.

chapters.title: Second Verse: What Was Promised
chapters.summary: Marta falters when the glass shows her drowned son; Serafina takes her line, and the hymn holds — but the presence pivots to Rafael, producing Aurel, alive, begging him to stop. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth made flesh in his brother's stolen face.

chapters.title: Third Verse: The Forgetting
chapters.summary: Rafael sings the third verse and feels himself being unwritten — Serafina looks through him, his own name slipping away — and understands Juno's choice from inside it. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: sacrifice rendered intimate and terrible.

chapters.title: Fourth Verse: What Was Chosen
chapters.summary: Instead of completing the erasure, Rafael alters the final line using Juno's own words — remembering instead of forgetting — and the hymn closes the breach on a chord of witness. The mirrors shatter outward. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: climax; truth rewrites the ritual's terms.

chapters.title: The Unreflected Man
chapters.summary: The house is silent and ordinary; Rafael survives but casts no reflection anywhere, and strangers' eyes slide off him. Only those who sang with him can see and remember him. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: bittersweet cost — he is now the forgotten founder.

chapters.title: Documentation Is a Kind of Prayer
chapters.summary: Epilogue: Rafael finishes the ledger, writes all four servants' names back into the record, and leaves the hymnal open on the chapel lectern for whoever comes next. Serafina pours two cups of tea, sets one before an empty chair, and speaks to him anyway. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: resolution — memory freely given defeats inheritance bought with silence.
